For finitely coded rational-semialgebraic covariance regions, \(\text{CertificateInferenceHandle}\) terminates, computes the exact full union \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\), retains the finite-sample coverage implication, and returns that full code only after a clean universal five-margin audit; otherwise it returns \(\mathsf{ABSTAIN}\).  For rational population covariances, finite rational-polynomial sentences decide whether the compatibility output is empty, a singleton, or has at least two elements.  A feasible candidate with zero affine separation forces abstention.  The certificates are written globally in the entries of the normalized matrix, so no normalization chart is required; auxiliary finite rational-semialgebraic charts may be changed by adjoining their polynomial graph and denominator-sign cells before projection, without changing the resulting matrix-space set.

On every simultaneous honest-slot coverage outcome on which the audit releases, the effectively computable constants in \(\text{def:audited-release-contraction}\) satisfy
\[
 r_{n,\alpha,H}\leq r_0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha,D)
 \leq C_0r_{n,\alpha,H},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha)
 \leq2C_0r_{n,\alpha,H},
\]
where
\[
 L_0=(p!\,\overline\kappa^{p-1})^{1/p},\qquad
 K_0=\frac{6\overline M}{\gamma _0}\sqrt{p(p-1)(1+L_0^2)},
 \qquad C_0=16K_0L_0^3,
\]

defs.def:certificate-inference-handle:
Fix a realized encoded region family, \(n\geq1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and rational thresholds \(\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0>0\) and \(\overline\kappa,\overline M\geq1\). For each \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\), introduce a candidate tuple
\[
w=(K,A,\Psi,(t_e)_{e\in K},(\Gamma_e)_{e\in K}).
\]
The full feasibility formula \(F_K(w)\) is the conjunction of: each encoded region formula at \(\Gamma_e\); \(\Gamma_e\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\); \(A_{ii}=1\); \((\det A)^2>0\); \(1-\pi_C(A)>0\) and \(1+\pi_C(A)>0\) for every directed simple cycle \(C\), where \(\pi_C(A)\) is the corresponding entry product in \(I_p-A\); \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\); \(t_{ej}\geq0\); and
\[
A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)
\qquad(e\in K).
\]
For such a tuple set \(\zeta(w)=1-\max_C|\pi_C(A)|\), \(\kappa(w)=\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\),
\[
\lambda(w)=\min\left\{\lambda_{\min}(\Psi),\min_{e\in K}\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma_e)\right\},
\qquad
M(w)=1+\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in K}\|\Gamma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in K}\|\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and, writing
\[
\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)=
\det\begin{pmatrix}
1&t_{ek}&t_{e\ell}\\
1&t_{fk}&t_{f\ell}\\
1&t_{gk}&t_{g\ell}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
set \(\gamma(w)=0\) if \(h-c<3\), and otherwise set
\[
\gamma(w)=
\min_{1\leq k<\ell\leq p}
\min_{\substack{S\subseteq K\\|S|=h-c}}
\max_{e<f<g\in S}|\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)|.
\]
The certificate procedure forms
\[
\Phi_{\mathcal U}(A)
=\bigvee_{\substack{K\subseteq E\\|K|=h}}
\exists\Psi\,\exists(t_e)_{e\in K}\,\exists(\Gamma_e)_{e\in K} F_K(w),
\]
calls effective real quantifier elimination to obtain a quantifier-free rational-polynomial code in \(A\), and calls it again on the closed sentence asserting that some feasible tuple violates at least one of
\[
\gamma(w)\geq\gamma_0,\qquad
\zeta(w)\geq\zeta_0,\qquad
\lambda(w)\geq\lambda_0,\qquad
\kappa(w)\leq\overline\kappa,\qquad
M(w)\leq\overline M.
\]
It returns the code for \(\Phi_{\mathcal U}\) when that sentence is false and returns \(\mathsf{ABSTAIN}\) when it is true. This definition names the finite symbolic procedure and its candidate margins; exactness, termination, coverage, and the abstention guarantee are asserted only by the theorem.
defs.def:encoded-covariance-regions:
A rational semialgebraic region code in dimension \(p\) is a finite list of polynomials in the \(p(p+1)/2\) independent entries of a symmetric matrix \(G\), with coefficients in \(\mathbb Q\), together with a finite Boolean formula \(\rho(G)\) whose atoms are comparisons of those polynomials with zero. Its realization is
\[
\operatorname{Real}(\rho)
=\{G\in\mathbb S_{++}^p:\rho(G)\}.
\]
An encoded covariance-region family supplies, for every \(n\geq1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and \(e\in E\), such a finite code \(\rho^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) and requires
\[
\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}
=\operatorname{Real}\bigl(\rho^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\bigr)\neq\varnothing.
\]
The code may be random through the sample, but after a sample outcome is fixed it is a finite rational string and its displayed equality with the region is exact, not an outer approximation or a membership oracle.
defs.def:compatible-set: For \(\Sigma\in(\mathbb S_{+}^{p})^{E}\), \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{A\in\mathcal D:\exists K\subseteq E,\ |K|\ge h,\ \exists\Psi\in\mathbb S_{+}^p,\ \exists t_e\in[0,\infty)^p,\ \Sigma_e=A^{-1}(\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e))A^{-\mathsf T}\ \forall e\in K\}\).
defs.def:subset-consensus: Definitional implementation note: given a feasibility oracle that returns the full solution set for each queried semialgebraic system, query every \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\) for all \(A\in\mathcal D\) satisfying \(\operatorname{offdiag}(A(\Sigma_e-\Sigma_f)A^{\mathsf T})=0\) for \(e,f\in K\) and admitting one \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_{+}^p\) with nonnegative diagonal shifts for the transformed raw covariances. Define \(\text{SubsetConsensus}(\Sigma,c)\) as the union of the oracle-returned solution sets. This enumeration makes exactly \(\binom{m}{h}\) oracle queries and, by expansion of \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), its returned union equals \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\); neither fact is a theorem contribution or a claim that an encoded terminating solver is supplied.
defs.def:confidence-union:
For each \(n\geq1\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), let \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) be the nonempty realization of its code in \(\text{def:encoded-covariance-regions}\). Define
\[
\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}
=\bigcup_{\substack{\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\\ e\in E}}
\mathcal R_c(\Gamma).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\) is the set-valued inversion of the encoded simultaneous covariance regions through the population replacement-compatibility map \(\mathcal R_c\). Coverage, computability, margin auditing, and singleton conclusions are theorem properties and are not included in this construction definition.

defs.def:audited-release-contraction:
Fix \(p,m,c\), put \(h=m-c\) and \(q=m-2c=h-c\), and fix rational thresholds \(\gamma _0,\zeta _0,\lambda _0>0\) and \(\overline\kappa,\overline M\geq1\).  Define
\[
 L_0=\bigl(p!\,\overline\kappa^{\,p-1}\bigr)^{1/p},\qquad
 K_0=\frac{6\overline M}{\gamma _0}
 \sqrt{p(p-1)(1+L_0^2)},
\]
\[
 \rho _0=\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{2K_0\overline M}\right\},
 \qquad C_0=16K_0L_0^3.
\]
These are effectively represented positive real algebraic numbers.

Let \(\mathfrak T\) be the finite union, over \(H_1,H_2\subseteq E\) with \(|H_1|=|H_2|=h\) and \(S\subseteq H_1\cap H_2\) with \(|S|=q\), of tuples
\[
 \tau=\bigl(H_1,H_2,S,D,U,\Omega,(s_e,\Sigma_e)_{e\in H_1},
 A,V,\Psi,(t_e,\Gamma_e)_{e\in H_2}\bigr)
\]
where \(D,U,A,V\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\), the matrices \(\Omega,\Psi,\Sigma_e,\Gamma_e\) are symmetric \(p\times p\) matrices, and \(s_e,t_e\in\mathbb R^p\), satisfying the following closed constraints.  The inverse variables obey \(DU=UD=I_p\) and \(AV=VA=I_p\).  Both \(D\) and \(A\) have unit diagonal; for every directed simple cycle \(C\), the corresponding products in \(I_p-D\) and \(I_p-A\) have absolute value at most \(1-\zeta _0\); and
\[
 \|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|U\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline\kappa,
 \qquad
 \|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|V\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline\kappa.
\]
The nuisance and covariance matrices and the shifts satisfy
\[
 \Omega,\Psi\succeq\lambda _0I_p,qquad
 \Sigma_e,\Gamma_e\succeq\lambda _0I_p,qquad
 s_e,t_e\in[0,\infty)^p,
\]
\[
 D\Sigma_eD^{\mathsf T}=\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\quad(e\in H_1),
 \qquad
 A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\quad(e\in H_2).
\]
Each of the two shift designs has affine separation at least \(\gamma _0\), with the separation computed using all subsets of its honest set having cardinality \(q\), and each side satisfies its scale bound
\[
 1+\|\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+
 \max_{e\in H_1}\|\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+
 \max_{e\in H_1}\|\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline M,
\]
\[
 1+\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm{op}}+
 \max_{e\in H_2}\|\Gamma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+
 \max_{e\in H_2}\|\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline M.
\]
All operator-norm, eigenvalue, and finite minimum--maximum conditions here are interpreted through their equivalent first-order real-polynomial formulas.  Define the full covariance-equation residual on the overlap by
\[
 \mathfrak r(\tau)=
 \max_{e\in S}
 \left\|A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}-\Psi-\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\right\|_{\mathrm F},
\]
and let \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\) be the subfamily satisfying
\[
 \|AU-I_p\|_{\mathrm F}\geq\rho _0.
\]
Set \(\mu _0=1\) if \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}=\varnothing\), and otherwise set
\[
 \mu _0=\min_{\tau\in\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}}\mathfrak r(\tau).
\]
Starting with \(j=1,2,\ldots\), use effective real quantifier elimination to decide whether some \(\tau\in\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\) has \(\mathfrak r(\tau)<2^{-j}\), and let \(\underline\mu=2^{-j}\) at the first negative answer.  Finally define
\[
 r_0=\frac{\underline\mu}{2\sqrt p\,L_0^2}.
\]
The package consisting of \(L_0,K_0,\rho _0,C_0,\mathfrak T,\mu _0,\underline\mu,r_0\) is \(\operatorname{AuditedReleaseContraction}(p,m,c,\gamma _0,\zeta _0,\lambda _0,\overline\kappa,\overline M)\).  Positivity and termination of the search are theorem properties, not part of this definition.

\[
